title: Seats nobody marked
prompt:
A theatre has 240 seats numbered 1 to 240. An usher puts a ribbon on every seat whose number is a multiple of 6, and a cushion on every seat whose number is a multiple of 10. Some seats get both.

How many seats get no ribbon and no cushion?
hints: How many numbers from 1 to 240 are multiples of 6, and how many are multiples of 10?
Which numbers are multiples of both 6 and 10, and did you count each of them twice?
Once you know how many numbers get at least one of the two, how many of the 240 are left over?
solution:
**184.**

From 1 to 240 there are 40 multiples of 6 (240 ÷ 6, rounded down) and 24 multiples of 10. A number is a multiple of both exactly when it is a multiple of 30, the least common multiple. It is not 6 × 10 = 60, because 6 and 10 share a factor. There are 8 of those.

Those 8 numbers were counted twice, once in each list, so the numbers with at least one are 40 + 24 − 8 = 56. Everything else gets neither: 240 − 56 = **184**.

The common slip is forgetting the overlap, which gives 176: it takes the shared numbers away twice.
